title: Dynamic Range Auto
body: Dynamic range lets a recipe hold highlights by exposing lower and lifting the picture back, as the camera's DR200 and DR400 do. It now has **Auto**, which picks DR100 or DR200 (or DR400 when the ceiling allows) from how much of the scene is close to clipping.

The measure is the share of the frame whose brightest channel is at or above 90% of DR100's white, on a 256-pixel grid. It uses the brightest channel rather than brightness because a saturated blue sky clips in blue long before it looks bright.

It was calibrated on 35 frames: sun-and-shade and blown-sky scenes measure 2.6–35% and go to DR200, evenly lit scenes stay at DR100, and so does a colour chart. In the viewfinder it waits 0.5 s before stepping up and 1.5 s before stepping down, so it doesn't flicker. A RAW is measured from its own decode, and a Cine take locks its choice at the start.

images.alt: A colour chart on a wooden table at DR100, DR200 and DR400, the camera's renders above Fonder's.
images.caption: DSCF6535, indoors at ISO 800: the camera's DR100, DR200 and DR400 conversions (top) and Fonder's (bottom). Nothing on the chart clips, so the three should look almost the same, and on both sides they do.
